title: Save instructions keep the user's plan, done-with items and rejected options
acceptance: Rule 1 (user's plan first): SAVE_INSTRUCTIONS in src/ai_checkpoint/schema.py tells the saver that when the user stated their own plan for what comes next, `next_steps` must START with that plan in the user's own words, every part, in the user's order, before any steps the AI adds. It contains the phrases "user's own words" (or "user's words") and "in order" (or "in the user's order"), and names `next_steps`.

Rule 1 (identifiable in the brief): the instruction tells the saver to prefix each such step with a fixed literal marker, `User's plan:` (exact text, quoted in the instruction), so the resume brief's 'Next steps' list shows which steps are the user's without any change to brief.py. FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["next_steps"] also mentions the user's plan coming first and the `User's plan:` marker.

Rule 2 (done-with items listed): SAVE_INSTRUCTIONS tells the saver to ALSO list items no longer needed, marked `done_with`, rather than leaving them out, and names the four examples: abandoned folders with their full path, old file names after a rename, connectors/tools no longer used, and env var NAMES that were used. The text contains "done_with", "full path", "rename" and "env var" (names only, never values, still stated). FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["workspace"] says done-with items must be listed too, not dropped.

Rule 2 (checklist unchanged): only `still_relevant` items appear in the brief's 'Set up first' checklist; a checkpoint whose workspace has a done_with folder and a done_with env var renders a brief whose 'Set up first' section contains neither (brief.py `_setup_first` unchanged; `git diff --stat src/ai_checkpoint/brief.py` is empty).

Rule 3 (rejected always filled): SAVE_INSTRUCTIONS tells the saver that EVERY decision where alternatives were discussed must list them in `rejected`, even when the reason is short or the option was only mentioned. Text contains "every decision" (case-insensitive) and "even when" near `rejected`. FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["decisions.rejected"] carries the same rule (no longer reads as freely optional when alternatives were discussed).
Wording stays short: SAVE_DESCRIPTION grows by no more than ~900 bytes over the old 2279, and the three rules are each one bullet (new or amended) in SAVE_INSTRUCTIONS.

Eval compaction prompt carries the rules: `compaction_system_prompt()` contains SAVE_INSTRUCTIONS verbatim and each updated FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS text, so it includes `User's plan:`, `done_with` with "full path", and the every-decision `rejected` rule (existing test_compaction_prompt_uses_save_instructions_and_field_descriptions passes; a new test asserts the three key phrases appear in the prompt).

MCP tool description updated: the registered `save_checkpoint` tool description (create_server().list_tools()) equals the new SAVE_DESCRIPTION and contains the three key phrases; field descriptions in the tool schema for next_steps, workspace and decisions.rejected equal the new FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS (test_mcp_tool_descriptions_come_from_schema_module passes).

Pinned hash tests updated deliberately: `_HEAD_SAVE_DESCRIPTION_SHA256` and `_HEAD_SAVE_DESCRIPTION_LEN` in tests/test_eval.py hold the new values, with a comment recording the previous values (sha 0b89d3ba..., len 2279) and why they changed (three gaps from eval-runs/2026-10-09-handover-v2-haiku); the paragraph-break assertion (`...can follow without asking.\n\nPick a short, descriptive` or its updated equivalent) still holds.

No format/store/MCP-tool change: `git diff --stat` touches only src/ai_checkpoint/schema.py and tests (plus optional docs/README wording); model.py, store.py, brief.py and the tool's parameter list are unchanged; COMPACTION_FIELDS types are unchanged.

Old checkpoints unchanged (regression): tests/fixtures/old_format_cp.json still loads and renders byte-identical to tests/fixtures/old_format_brief.golden.md (tests/test_rejected.py golden tests pass; fixture files unmodified per `git status`).

FakeModel compaction still validates: running the offline eval with FakeModel (e.g. tests in tests/test_eval.py / test_runner.py that build compaction handovers) produces a checkpoint that passes validation with no ValidationError.
Full suite passes: `$HOME/aic-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` reports all tests passing (baseline 307 passed; count may only increase).
